2  JUDGMENT

By way of this petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioner has prayed for the following reliefs:-
"It is, therefore, prayed that the appeal may kindly be allowed Judicial Magistrate, r to and order dated 7.5.2018, passed by the learned Chief Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh in Application No. 247/4 of 2018/2015, in main Case No. 119-1 of 2009, titled Food Inspector versus Kamal Soni, filed under Section 20(A) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, whereby present petitioner has been ordered to be impleaded as accused/respondent No.2 in the main case, may be quashed and set-aside along with all consequential proceedings thereto, against the petitioner."

2. Brief facts necessary for the adjudication of the present petition are as under:-
A complaint was filed under Section 7(i) and 7(ii) 2(ia) (a), 2(ix) (k), 16(1) (a)(ii) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1944, (hereinafter to be referred to as '1954 Act') and Rules made there-under against one Sh. Kamal Soni and Rajinder Chaddha on the ground that Double Distilled Spiced Country Liquor "Patiala Orange" Brand,
which was .
lifted by the complainant from L-14 shop, Unit No. III, near Luhnu ground, Raura Sector, Bilaspur, H.P., of which Mr. Kamal Soni was the salesman and Mr. Rajinder Chaddha was the vendor, was found to be misbranded as also adulterated.
3. During the pendency of this complaint, Shri Rajinder Chaddha expired.

Thereafter, an application was filed by Sh. Kamal Soni, the other accused, under Section 20-A of the 1954 Act, praying therein that the present petitioner be impleaded as accused being the manufacturer, distributor/dealer of the product in issue inter-alia on the ground that the vendor-accused had already died and the trial against the salesman may be vitiated as the manufacturer has not been impleaded as a party.
4.

Record demonstrates that the response which was filed to the said application by the Food Safety Officer was to the effect that the application filed by Sh. Kamal Soni was not maintainable as the applicant had not submitted the written warranty in the form of bills/invoice of purchase from the dealer or distributor before the Court and thus had failed to fulfill the legal mandatory provisions as contained in Section 19(2) of the 1954 Act.
5. By way of the impugned order, the application to implead the present petitioner as an accused was allowed by the learned Trial Court .
by observing that as accused No.2 had died and applicant (Kamal Soni) was unable to obtain the receipt with regard to the liquor sold by him, therefore, the manufacturer needs to be impleaded as proper party in the case.

3 6.
I have heard learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner as well as learned Additional General for the State.
7. Respondent No. 2 Sh. Kamal Soni despite being served did not appear before the Court.

Having carefully perused the impugned order as well as the documents appended with the petition as also the statutory preventions of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, this Court is the considered view that the impugned order is not sustainable in the eyes of law.

Section 20-A of the Act, in which the application was filed by sSh. Kamal Soni for impleading the present petitioner as an accused in the trial, provides as under:-
"20-A. Power of Court to implead manufacturer etc:

Where at any time during the trial of any offence under this Act alleged to have been committed by any person, not being the manufacturer, distributor or dealer of any article of food, the Court is satisfied, on the evidence adduced before it, that such manufacturer, distributor or dealer is lso concerned with the offence, then the court may notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (3) of section 319 of the Code of .
Criminal Procedure, 1973 [2 of 1974] or in Section 20 proceed against him as though a prosecution had been instituted against him under Section 20."
8.

A perusal of the contents of Section 20-A of the Act thus demonstrates that a manufacturer,
distributor or dealer can be impleaded as an accused in a trial by the Court but provided the Court is satisfied on the evidence adduced before it that such manufacturer, distributor or dealer is also concerned with that offence.

In the present case, no such finding has been returned by the learned Court below that on the strength of evidence adduced before it, it was satisfied that the present petitioner was also involved in the commission of the alleged offence.

Simply because, one of the accused was dead and the other accused was unable to obtain the sale receipt, on this count alone,
the learned Trial Court was not justified in impleading the present petitioner as an accused in the case that too by holding that the manufacturer was a proper party because this is not the requirement of Section 20-A of the Act.
The requirement is satisfaction of the Court on evidence adduced before it that such manufacturer, distributor or dealer is also concerned with the offence.

9. Accordingly, as the order which has been passed by the learned Court below does not passes the test of Section 20-A of the 1954 Act, this petition is allowed as prayed for and the impugned order passed by the Court of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bilaspur, dated .
07.05.2018, in the application filed under Section 20-A of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act,
1954, vide which the present petitioner was ordered to be impleaded as an accused in the trial, is ordered to be quashed and set-aside.
The petition stands disposed of in the above terms, so also the miscellaneous application(s), if any.

(Ajay Mohan Goel) Judge March 31, 2022 (chander)
